# Synthesia hits $4B valuation, lets employees cash out
British startup Synthesia, whose AI platform helps companies create interactive training videos, has raised a $200 million Series E round of funding that brings its valuation to $4 billion — up from $2.1 billion just a year ago.

data.description:
# Synthesia (company)
## History
### Funding
Synthesia gained a total valuation of $1 billion, and achieved [unicorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorn_(finance)) status, when it raised $90 million from [Accel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accel_(company)) and [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia) partnership NVentures, in June 2023, during its Series C funding round.

Counting 60,000 customers by January 2025, including over 60% of Fortune 100 companies; the company raised $180 million in a Series D round led by [NEA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Enterprise_Associates),[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-Reuters25-38) with new investors World Innovation Lab (WiL), [Atlassian Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlassian) and PSP Growth, as well as existing investors [GV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GV_(company)), MMC Ventures and [FirstMark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FirstMark_Capital), doubling Synthesia's valuation to $2.1 billion. [[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-Times-40) Capital raised by 2025 had reached $330 million,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-Times-40) with investments slated to further product innovation, talent growth, and company expansion in [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America), [Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan) and [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia).

In April 2025, [Adobe Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Inc.) invested £10 million in the company for a strategic partnership. [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-prescott2025a-1) With a revenue stream then exceeding $100 million annually; GV led a Series E funding round in October 2025, resulting in Synthesia's $4 billion valuation,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesia_(company)#cite_note-42) raising $200 million from GV, Nvidia and Accel to develop, in 2026, interactive audio-visual avatar "agents" that converse on topic, for automated sales training and corporate communications, such as recruiting.

The company crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in April 2025, following a strategic partnership with Adobe.
Synthesia raised a $200 million Series E funding round in January 2026 at a $4 billion post-money valuation, nearly doubling its $2.1 billion valuation from the $180 million Series D in early 2025. Investors like GV and NVIDIA back Synthesia as an application-layer AI company turning foundational models into enterprise tools for video and learning. The company serves major clients like Bosch, Merck, SAP, and Microsoft, offering a freemium model alongside subscription and enterprise plans. It focuses on reducing the need for traditional video production in corporate learning and development.
In January 2025, Synthesia raised $180 million in a Series D funding round led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA), achieving a post-money valuation of $2.1 billion. Investors included Accel, Kleiner Perkins, PSP Growth, and others from the queried list. This followed a $90 million Series C in 2023 at $1 billion valuation. By April 2025, shortly after the round, Synthesia crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) and reported quadrupling large contracts over $100,000 in the prior 12 months, on track for $200 million ARR that year.
The Series D supported ongoing growth in AI video tools. A subsequent $200 million Series E in early 2026, led by GV with participation from NEA, Accel, Kleiner Perkins, PSP Growth, MMC Ventures, and new investors like Evantic and Hedosophia, doubled valuation to $4 billion. Funds fueled development of conversational AI agents for interactive training, role-playing, and upskilling. The company also introduced an employee secondary sale via Nasdaq.
Synthesia's traction stems from enterprise demand for scalable, interactive learning amid AI advancements and workforce reskilling pressures. CEO Victor Riparbelli highlighted the convergence of capable AI agents and market needs for internal knowledge sharing. | Synthesia funding rounds

# AI Video Startup Synthesia Valued At $4 Billion In New $200 Million Raise
Forbes Staff

London-based AI video generation startup Synthesia has closed a funding round that nearly doubles its valuation to $4 billion, three sources familiar with the matter told _Forbes_.

The company last [raised](https://www.forbes.com/sites/iainmartin/2025/01/15/this-ai-avatar-startup-raised-180-million-to-make-corporate-videos-less-boring/) $180 million at a $2.1 billion valuation in January.
